lawyer: Md. Mohammad Yasin Khan, Advocate —For the Petitioners.
parties:
Haji Esob Ali & others  ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Rahiz Miah and others  ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
8. It is the case of the learned Advocate that the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law allowing addition under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure instead of recording an order of abatement as heirs of deceased plaintiff No. 3 were not substituted within 90 days of the death of the plaintiff No.3. The court without deciding the actual date of the death of plaintiff No. 3 and without considering whether they have filed this application within time or not the court allowed this application by committing an error of law without considering the written objection. The court erred in law in not holding that after 90 days from the date of death of plaintiff No. 3 the abatement is automatic under law and unless the abatement is set aside within 60 days the addition would be an illegality. The application for substitution was made after 24 months of the death of plaintiff No.3 and subsequent application for addition as plaintiff also was made after 25 months and 5 days and in the absence of any specific prayer claiming the benefit of section 5 of the Limitation Act the applications are completely time barred and it is the well established principle of law that the court cannot grant any relief not sought for. This court allowed this addition by committing an error of law and this present case does not fall within the provision of Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The court did not apply its judicial mind to the relevant facts of the application, written objection and the law applicable. The learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice not exercising a discretion fairly and rightly because nothing has been considered which was submitted against the plaintiff opposite parties in passing the impugned order. The court also did not find that opposite parties 3 to 10 were prevented by sufficient cause for not applying in time to have been substituted or added as plaintiff. 

 10. In the instant case, it is an admitted position that opposite parties 3 to 10 are the sons and wife of Abdul Malek and filed initially an application for substitution in place of deceased Abdul Malek who admittedly was alive when the suit was instituted by him along with others. A court of law would allow a substitution claimed whether of the deceased plaintiff or deceased defendant occasioned after the suit was instituted even after setting aside abatement if the court is satisfied as to the just cause of delay in bringing the application for substitution before the court. Under the provision of law, a party who may be the heirs of a plaintiff or a defendant can also be added as a party as heirs of any defendant or plaintiff under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This provision of the Code of Civil Procedure deals with the addition of parties, necessary parties or proper parties by the court at any time of the proceeding and even before the judgment is delivered by a court of law. This is a very wide power but this discretion is to be exercised by the court in adding parties whether they are necessary parties or proper parties or addition of parties in case of death of any plaintiff or defendant during the pendency of the suit but brought to the notice of the court within the time of limitation. This limitation law is not an absolute bar because it can be condoned under section 5 of the Limitation Act even when it is the specific claim or not but evidently explained from the facts of the case.
